cold_open_hook: Rain at Interlagos, a title for Mercedes, and a brand new Formula E car on track today.

stories.speaker: pixie
stories.headline: Norris masters the Interlagos rain
stories.angle: A calm win from pole in weather that kept changing; the real drama was behind him.
facts: Lando Norris won the Sao Paulo Grand Prix from pole by 14.6 seconds.
The weather kept changing through the 71-lap race.
Kimi Antonelli jumped Norris at the start and led until the first stops.
No one crashed out and there was no safety car.
Charles Leclerc got a five-second penalty for forcing Liam Lawson wide, which handed seventh to Lawson.

stories.speaker: pixie
stories.headline: A new era rolls out at Jarama
stories.angle: Formula E's most powerful car runs as a full grid for the first time.
facts: The whole Formula E grid tests at Circuito de Madrid Jarama from 16 to 20 November.
It is the GEN4 car's first collective test; the series calls it its most advanced and powerful car.
Season 13 has 21 races at 13 events in 11 countries.
It opens with a night double-header in Jeddah on 18 and 19 December.
Opel joins as a new manufacturer.

stories.speaker: byte
stories.headline: Camara's surprise home debut
stories.angle: Byte: a Brazilian rookie at home, and two Brazilians on the grid again.
facts: Rafael Camara, 21, a Ferrari Academy driver signed to Haas for 2027, made his Grand Prix debut in Sao Paulo.
Haas had confirmed Esteban Ocon would not return.
With Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto also racing, Brazil had two home drivers in an F1 race for the first time since 2016.

stories.speaker: pixie
stories.headline: Alan Jones, 1946-2026
stories.angle: A respectful farewell: Williams' first world champion.
facts: Alan Jones died on 5 November, aged 80, after a short illness.
He won 12 Grands Prix between 1975 and 1986.
Five wins in 1980 brought him the title in the Williams FW07B, the team's first.
He remains the last Australian to win the championship.
